question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{4x+1}-2.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{4x+1}-2
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{4y+1}-2.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\sqrt[3]{4y+1}-2 \\ \sqrt[3]{4y+1} & =x+2 \\ {(\sqrt[3]{4y+1})}^{3} & ={(x+2)}^{3} \\ 4y+1 & =(x+2)^{3} \\ 4y & =(x+2)^{3}-1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}.
$$
